title: 3Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

You may return the triplets in any order.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2] = (-1) + 0 + 1 = 0. nums[1] + nums[2] + nums[4] = 0 + 1 + (-1) = 0. nums[0] + nums[3] + nums[4] = (-1) + 2 + (-1) = 0. The distinct triplets are [-1,0,1] and [-1,-1,2]. The order of the output and the order within triplets do not matter.
The only possible triplet does not sum up to 0.
The only possible triplet sums up to 0.

approach: After sorting, fix nums[i] and search the suffix with two pointers. A sum below zero requires a larger left value; a sum above zero requires a smaller right value. Skip equal fixed values and equal pointer values after a match to emit each value triplet once. Time complexity is O(n^2), dominated by the n two-pointer scans after O(n log n) sorting.
